Decision (Recommended): Start with PowerShell for speed; prepare Terraform modules in parallel for long-term
Options Considered: PowerShell only | Terraform only | Hybrid (PS now → TF later)
Rationale: Fastest path to a PoC while paving a path to standardized IaC and state mgmt later
Notes: Define a 1:1 TF module map for future parity

Decision (Recommended): Use OIDC-based ADO service connection (secretless)
Options Considered: OIDC (Workload Identity) | Service Principal secret | Managed Identity (self-hosted agent)
Rationale: Removes secrets, least management overhead, strong security posture
Notes: Fallback to SP secret only if OIDC blocked

Decision (Recommended): Azure Storage remote state with locks; per-environment containers
Options Considered: Local state | Azure Storage state | Terraform Cloud
Rationale: Reliable locking, RBAC, encryption-at-rest; fits enterprise controls

Decision (Recommended): Use SHIR (v5.56) in hub; reserve Azure IR for internal/MPE cases
Options Considered: SHIR only | Azure IR (Managed VNet) | Mixed
Rationale: SHIR reaches many client PGs over existing peering; supports UAMI with PG v2.0

Decision (Recommended): Use existing VNet peering; no MPE, no public IPs
Options Considered: Peering | Managed Private Endpoints | Public allowlist
Rationale: Peering already in place; avoids per-client PE approvals and public exposure

Decision (Recommended): User-Assigned Managed Identity (UAMI) for Script activity
Options Considered: UAMI | SPN (client secret/cert) | DB user/password
Rationale: Passwordless, centrally managed, least-privilege via Entra; aligns with zero-secret goal

Decision (Recommended): Link client Private DNS zones to hub; fallback to Azure DNS Private Resolver
Options Considered: Zone linking | Private Resolver + forwarding | Hosts overrides
Rationale: Most maintainable; keeps FQDNs intact; Private Resolver only if linking not possible

Decision (Recommended): 2 nodes (N+1), auto-update on; scale-out if throughput requires
Options Considered: 1 node | 2 nodes | 3+ nodes
Rationale: Resilience against single node failure; maintenance-friendly

Decision (Recommended): Windows Server 2022, no public IP; patch via Update Mgmt; minimal egress
Options Considered: Public IP + RDP | Bastion | No public, JIT
Rationale: Reduces attack surface; consistent with platform standards

Decision (Recommended): Azure Repos; Git only in Dev; PR-based promotion to Test/Prod
Options Considered: Azure Repos | GitHub | No Git
Rationale: Matches existing ADO; keeps prod clean and deploy-only

Decision (Recommended): Multi-stage YAML pipeline with environment approvals
Options Considered: Classic release | Single-stage | Multi-stage YAML
Rationale: Traceable, reusable, easier approvals and conditions

Decision (Recommended): Key Vault for any non-AAD secrets; ADF references KV
Options Considered: Key Vault | ADF secure strings | Inline in code (avoid)
Rationale: Centralized governance, rotation, and RBAC

Decision (Recommended): Allow public access but restrict by firewall while PoC; plan for Private Endpoint later
Options Considered: Public (restricted) | Private Endpoint | Public open
Rationale: No client-side PE approvals needed for PoC; roadmap to PE for strict isolation later

Decision (Recommended): ADLS Gen2 per env; container 'logs' for pipeline results
Options Considered: Shared account | Per-env accounts | None
Rationale: Clear isolation and lifecycle mgmt; cheap, simple evidence trail

Decision (Recommended): Send ADF diagnostics to Log Analytics; alerts for pipeline failure & IR heartbeat
Options Considered: LAW + Alerts | Storage logs only | None
Rationale: Actionable telemetry and alerting path for ops

Decision (Recommended): Script activity → Postgres LS (UAMI via SHIR); optional write to ADLS
Options Considered: Function runner | Copy-only | Manual client tool
Rationale: Directly validates UAMI + network; minimal moving parts

Decision (Recommended): Least-priv RBAC: scoped roles for UAMI; ADF Contributor for CI/CD; PIM for elevation
Options Considered: Broad Owner rights | Least-priv + PIM | Custom roles
Rationale: Balance of security and operability; auditable changes

Decision (Recommended): Adopt corporate standard; include env, app, owner, cost center tags
Options Considered: Ad-hoc | Corporate standard | Minimal tags
Rationale: Discoverability, cost mgmt, and policy compliance

Decision (Recommended): Two SHIR nodes; idempotent infra scripts; ADF export for rebuild
Options Considered: Single node | Multi-node + backups | Active-active regions
Rationale: Meets PoC RTO/RPO without overbuild
Notes: Consider multi-region only if required later

Decision (Recommended): Gates before SHIR install and first client run
Options Considered: No gates | Single final gate | Stage-level gates
Rationale: Prevents accidental client impact; ensures prerequisites are met

Decision (Recommended): Idempotent scripts; what-if checks; manual approval before destructive ops
Options Considered: Ad-hoc reverts | Full IaC with plans | Script-based with guards
Rationale: Reduces risk; makes changes predictable

Decision (Recommended): Require SSL; enforce latest TLS; set sslmode verify-full where possible
Options Considered: Prefer TLS | Allow non-SSL
Rationale: Meets security baselines; reduces MITM risk

Decision (Recommended): SHIR auto-update on; capture baseline; pin only if regressions occur
Options Considered: Auto-update | Pinned version | Mixed
Rationale: Keeps patches current with low overhead

Decision (Recommended): Store pipeline outputs & key logs in ADLS; 90-day retention (adjust per policy)
Options Considered: No retention | Short-term | Policy-aligned
Rationale: Supports reviews and troubleshooting

Decision (Recommended): Revisit PEs for Key Vault/Storage if clients standardize on PEs
Options Considered: No PEs | PEs for all | PEs selectively
Rationale: Enhances isolation if operationally feasible later
